scenario: A user needs BitLocker and the ability to join a company domain. Which Windows edition is the minimum?

options.note: No BitLocker management or domain join.

explanation: Windows 11 Pro is the minimum edition with BitLocker, domain join, Group Policy and Remote Desktop host. Home lacks domain join and BitLocker's full management. Enterprise and Education add more but aren't the minimum.

scenario: Which hardware requirement must a PC meet to install Windows 11?
explanation: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0 and UEFI with Secure Boot, plus a supported 64-bit CPU, 4 GB RAM and 64 GB storage. A legacy BIOS PC or one with TPM 1.2 fails the check.

scenario: Which command shows a Windows PC's IP address, DNS servers and MAC address?
explanation: ipconfig /all shows the IP address, mask, gateway, DNS servers, DHCP details and MAC address. Plain ipconfig shows only the basics, while /release, /renew and /flushdns change lease or cache rather than display.

scenario: Which command shows each router hop on the path to a destination?
explanation: tracert lists each router hop on the path and the latency to it, which helps find where traffic stops. Ping tests only end-to-end reachability. Linux and macOS use traceroute.

scenario: Which command tests DNS name resolution directly?
explanation: nslookup queries a DNS server directly for records, so it tests name resolution separately from connectivity. Ping to a name also resolves, but it mixes DNS with reachability.

scenario: Which command repairs corrupted Windows system files?
explanation: sfc /scannow scans protected system files and replaces damaged ones from the cached copy. If SFC can't repair, run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth to fix the component store first.

scenario: Which command checks a drive for file system errors and bad sectors?
explanation: chkdsk /r finds file system errors and locates bad sectors, recovering readable data. /f only fixes file system errors without scanning for bad sectors, so /r is the thorough option.

scenario: Which command applies new Group Policy settings immediately?
explanation: gpupdate /force reapplies all Group Policy settings immediately instead of waiting for the refresh cycle. gpresult shows what was applied, but doesn't apply anything.

scenario: Which command copies folders with options to mirror and retry, and is suited for large file copies?

options.note: Basic copy with verification; no mirroring.
Older copy tool; no mirror or retry options.

explanation: robocopy is the robust copy tool with mirroring (/mir), retries, resume and logging, ideal for large copies. xcopy and copy are simpler and lack those features.

scenario: Which tool shows running processes and CPU and memory use, and lets you end an unresponsive app?
explanation: Task Manager shows processes, CPU, memory, disk and network use, and lets you end unresponsive tasks and manage startup apps. Resource Monitor gives deeper detail but Task Manager is the first stop.

scenario: Which tool shows system, application and security logs to investigate errors?
explanation: Event Viewer shows application, system and security logs. Look for errors and warnings at the time of the problem and use the event ID to search for causes.

scenario: A device shows a yellow exclamation mark. Which tool is this in, and what does it mean?

options.text: Device Manager; a driver or device problem
Event Viewer; a security log entry

explanation: A yellow exclamation mark in Device Manager means the device has a driver or resource problem. Update, roll back or reinstall the driver, or check the device status. A down arrow means disabled.

scenario: Which tool creates, deletes and formats partitions with a graphical interface?
explanation: Disk Management is the GUI for initializing disks, creating, deleting and formatting partitions and assigning drive letters. Diskpart does the same from the command line.

scenario: Which tool is used to start, stop and set startup types for background services?
explanation: services.msc lists services and lets you start, stop and set the startup type: Automatic, Automatic (Delayed Start), Manual or Disabled. Task Manager only shows service status.

scenario: Which tool can start Windows in diagnostic or selective startup mode to troubleshoot?
explanation: msconfig offers diagnostic or selective startup and controls boot options such as Safe Boot. In current Windows, startup apps are managed from Task Manager, not msconfig.

scenario: Which file system should be used for a USB drive that must store files larger than 4 GB and work on Windows and macOS?
explanation: exFAT has no 4 GB file limit and works on both Windows and macOS, which suits flash drives. FAT32 caps files at 4 GB, and NTFS is read-only on macOS by default.

scenario: Which Windows file system supports file permissions and encryption with EFS?
explanation: NTFS supports file and folder permissions, EFS encryption, compression, quotas and journaling. FAT32 and exFAT have none of the permission features.

scenario: Which partition style supports drives larger than 2 TB and is required for UEFI boot on Windows 11?

options.note: Limited to 2 TB and four primary partitions.
A file system, not a partition style.

explanation: GPT supports disks over 2 TB and many partitions, and is required for UEFI boot in Windows 11. MBR is limited to 2 TB and four primary partitions.

scenario: Which type of Windows installation keeps the user's files and apps while moving to a newer version?
explanation: An in-place upgrade moves to a newer Windows version and keeps files, apps and settings. A clean install erases the drive, so back up first.

scenario: Which macOS feature provides automatic backups to an external drive?

options.note: Cloud file sync, not local backups.

explanation: Time Machine automatically backs up a Mac to an external drive, keeping hourly, daily and weekly versions. iCloud syncs files but is not a full backup.

scenario: Which macOS feature encrypts the startup disk?
explanation: FileVault encrypts the macOS startup disk, like BitLocker on Windows. Keychain stores passwords and Gatekeeper checks app signatures.

scenario: Which macOS app stores passwords, certificates and secure notes?
explanation: Keychain Access stores passwords, certificates and secure notes on macOS, and iCloud Keychain syncs them across Apple devices. Time Machine is for backups.

scenario: Which Linux command shows the current working directory?
explanation: pwd prints the working directory. The other basics are ls (list), cd (change), cp (copy), mv (move or rename), rm (remove), mkdir (create folder) and cat (display file).

scenario: Which Linux command changes file permissions?
explanation: chmod changes file permissions, for example chmod 755 gives the owner read, write and execute, and others read and execute. chown changes the owner.

scenario: Which Linux command runs a single command with administrator (root) privileges?
explanation: sudo runs one command as root after you enter your own password, and logs it. su switches to another user, and chmod and chown change permissions and ownership.

scenario: Which command installs software on Ubuntu or Debian Linux?
explanation: apt install installs packages from repositories on Debian and Ubuntu. Red Hat-based systems use yum or dnf, and macOS commonly uses Homebrew.

scenario: Which Linux command searches text in files for a pattern?

options.note: Searches for files by name or attributes.

explanation: grep searches text for a pattern, for example grep error /var/log/syslog. find locates files by name or attribute, and cat only displays content.

scenario: Which Windows tool lets you edit Group Policy on a single Pro computer?
explanation: gpedit.msc opens the Local Group Policy Editor, available in Pro, Enterprise and Education but not Home. Domain-wide policy is managed from Active Directory.

scenario: Which Control Panel or Settings area changes which app opens a file type?
explanation: Default apps in Settings controls which program opens each file type or protocol. Assigning the wrong default is why a document opens in an unexpected program.

scenario: Which tool schedules a script to run every night at 2 AM on Windows?
explanation: Task Scheduler runs programs or scripts on a schedule or in response to triggers such as logon or an event. Services run continuously and don't schedule at specific times.

scenario: Which tool shows detailed information about hardware, drivers and system components?
explanation: msinfo32 (System Information) lists hardware, drivers and system components. dxdiag focuses on DirectX, display and sound.

scenario: Which Windows setting turns off automatic sleep when a laptop is plugged in?
explanation: Power settings (the power plan) control sleep, hibernate, display timeout and lid actions, separately for plugged in and battery. Set Sleep to Never for plugged in.

scenario: Which mobile OS lets users install apps from outside the official store (sideloading) more easily by default?

options.note: Restricted by default in most regions.

explanation: Android allows sideloading apps from unknown sources with a setting, while iOS restricts to the App Store by default. Sideloading raises malware risk, so allow it only when needed.

scenario: Which command restarts a Windows computer immediately?
explanation: shutdown /r /t 0 restarts immediately: /r restarts, /s shuts down, /t sets a delay in seconds. Use /a to abort a pending shutdown.

scenario: Which command maps a network share to a drive letter?
explanation: net use maps a network share to a drive letter, for example net use Z: \\server\share. Add /persistent:yes to keep it after restart.

scenario: A user gets an email claiming to be from their bank, asking them to click a link and log in. What is this?
explanation: Phishing uses fraudulent email to steal credentials. Related attacks: vishing (voice calls), smishing (text messages), whaling (executives) and spear phishing (targeted).

scenario: Someone follows an employee through a secure door without badging in. What is this?
explanation: Following someone through a secure door is tailgating. Access control vestibules, badge readers and training reduce it. Piggybacking is similar, with consent.

scenario: An attacker watches a user type their PIN at a coffee shop. What is this?
explanation: Watching someone enter a PIN or password is shoulder surfing. Privacy screen filters and awareness reduce the risk.

scenario: An attacker sets up a Wi-Fi network named like the coffee shop's to capture traffic. What is this?
explanation: An evil twin is a rogue access point that mimics a legitimate Wi-Fi name to intercept traffic. Use a VPN, verify the network and avoid sensitive logins on public Wi-Fi.

scenario: Files are encrypted and a message demands payment for the key. What type of malware is this?
explanation: Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment. Offline, tested backups are the best protection, and paying doesn't guarantee recovery.

scenario: Which malware hides deep in the operating system and is very hard to detect or remove?
explanation: A rootkit hides deep in the OS or firmware and conceals itself, so it may need a boot-time scan or an OS reinstall. A virus or worm doesn't hide this way.

scenario: Which malware records everything a user types?
explanation: A keylogger records keystrokes to steal passwords and sensitive data. Spyware gathers information more broadly, and ransomware encrypts.

scenario: A free game a user installed secretly opened a backdoor for attackers. What type of malware is this?
explanation: A Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software, such as a free game, while opening a backdoor. A worm self-replicates over the network without user action.

scenario: A PC's CPU is at 100% constantly and the fan is loud, but nothing obvious is running. Which malware is likely?
explanation: Constant 100% CPU use and a loud fan with nothing visible suggests a cryptominer using resources to mine coins. Check Task Manager for unfamiliar processes.

scenario: What is the first step in CompTIA's best-practice malware removal process?
explanation: Malware removal begins with identifying and verifying the symptoms. Then quarantine the system, disable System Restore, remediate, schedule scans, re-enable System Restore and educate the user.

scenario: Why should System Restore be disabled during malware removal?

options.text: Restore points may contain the malware

explanation: Restore points can contain copies of the malware, which could reinfect the PC if restored. Disable System Restore during cleaning, then re-enable it and create a new clean point.

scenario: What should a technician do with an infected PC before cleaning it?

options.text: Share its files with other users

explanation: Quarantine the infected PC by disconnecting it from the network (unplug Ethernet, disable Wi-Fi) so malware can't spread. Then clean it.

scenario: Which is the most secure Wi-Fi security setting?
explanation: WPA3 with AES is the most secure setting. WPA2-AES is acceptable, while WEP and WPA/TKIP are weak and should not be used.

scenario: A company wants employees to authenticate to Wi-Fi with their own network credentials through a central server. What should be used?
explanation: WPA3-Enterprise (or WPA2-Enterprise) uses 802.1X authentication with a RADIUS server so each user logs in with their own credentials. Personal mode uses one shared passphrase.

scenario: Which is an example of multifactor authentication?

options.text: A security question and a PIN

explanation: MFA combines different factor types: something you know (password), have (token, phone) or are (fingerprint). Two passwords or a password and a PIN are the same factor.

scenario: Which principle gives users only the permissions needed for their job?
explanation: Least privilege gives users only the permissions needed for their job. Use standard accounts for daily work and elevate to admin only when needed.

scenario: Which Windows feature prompts before changes that need administrator rights?
explanation: User Account Control prompts before changes that need admin rights, so malware can't silently modify the system. Turning it off is a security risk.

scenario: Which Windows feature encrypts an entire drive?
explanation: BitLocker encrypts an entire drive and uses the TPM, and BitLocker To Go covers removable drives. EFS encrypts individual files and folders instead.

scenario: A shared folder's share permission is Read, and the user's NTFS permission is Full Control. What access do they have over the network?
explanation: When share and NTFS permissions combine over the network, the most restrictive applies, so Read share permission limits the user to Read. Local access uses NTFS only.

scenario: Which built-in Windows tool provides antivirus and anti-malware protection?
explanation: Microsoft Defender is the built-in antivirus and anti-malware in Windows. Keep definitions updated and scan regularly.

scenario: Which physical security control uses two doors so only one person can enter at a time?
explanation: An access control vestibule (formerly mantrap) uses two interlocked doors so only one person enters at a time, preventing tailgating. A turnstile or guard provides different controls.

scenario: Which data destruction method is best for an old hard drive that must never be read again?

options.text: Deleting files and emptying the trash

explanation: Physical destruction, such as shredding or drilling, is best for drives that must never be read again. Degaussing works on magnetic drives but not SSDs, and a standard format leaves data recoverable.

scenario: A company wants to reuse old drives internally while making old data unrecoverable. What should it do?

options.text: Run a quick format on each drive

explanation: Overwriting (wiping) or the drive's secure erase command makes data unrecoverable while keeping the drive reusable. A quick format only removes pointers to data.

scenario: A website shows a certificate warning in the browser. What should the user do?

options.text: Not enter information and report it
Click through and log in quickly

explanation: A certificate warning can mean interception, expiry or a fake site, so don't enter data and report it. Clicking through the warning exposes you.

scenario: Which browser practice improves security?

options.text: Save passwords in a text file

explanation: Install only trusted extensions, keep the browser updated and use a password manager. Saving passwords in plain text or disabling updates weakens security.

scenario: A lost company phone contains sensitive email. What should the admin do first?

options.text: Remotely lock or wipe it with MDM
Wait to see if it's returned
Change the Wi-Fi password at home

explanation: For a lost company phone, remotely lock or wipe it with MDM to protect the data first. Locating it comes second.

scenario: Which mobile setting best protects a phone if it's stolen?
explanation: A strong screen lock (long PIN or biometric) with device encryption protects a stolen phone. Swipe-to-unlock offers no protection.

scenario: Which account type should be used for everyday work on a Windows PC?
explanation: Use a standard user account for daily work and an administrator account only for admin tasks. This limits damage if malware runs.

scenario: Which type of attack tries every possible password until one works?
explanation: Brute force tries every possible password until one works. Account lockout and long passwords defend against it, and a dictionary attack tries common words instead.

scenario: Which Windows feature lets users sign in with a face, fingerprint or PIN tied to the device?
explanation: Windows Hello supports passwordless sign-in with face, fingerprint or a device-bound PIN. The credential stays on the device with the TPM.

scenario: Which protocol is used for network authentication in Active Directory domains?
explanation: Kerberos authenticates users in Active Directory domains using tickets, so passwords aren't sent repeatedly. It needs synchronized clocks and works with TCP/UDP 88.

scenario: Which describes a zero-day vulnerability?

options.text: A flaw exploited before a patch exists
A bug fixed on the day it's found
A virus that runs at midnight
A patch released on day zero

explanation: A zero-day is a flaw exploited before the vendor has a patch. Defense in depth, segmentation and rapid patching reduce the risk, since no signature exists.

scenario: An employee gets a call from "IT support" asking for their password. What is this?
explanation: A phone call asking for a password is vishing (voice phishing). Real IT staff should never ask for your password, so hang up and report it.

scenario: Which security measure locks an account after several failed sign-in attempts?
explanation: An account lockout policy locks an account after a number of failed attempts, slowing brute-force attacks. A password expiration policy forces changes instead.

scenario: Which is an example of something you HAVE as an authentication factor?
explanation: A security key is something you have (possession). Smart cards and authenticator apps are possession factors too. A PIN is something you know, and a fingerprint is something you are.

scenario: A Windows PC shows a blue screen (BSOD) right after a new driver was installed. What should be tried first?

options.text: Use Safe Mode to roll back the driver

explanation: If a new driver causes a BSOD, boot into Safe Mode, which loads minimal drivers, and roll back or remove the driver. Reinstalling Windows is unnecessary.

scenario: Windows is slow, and Task Manager shows memory usage near 100%. What helps most?

options.text: Close unneeded apps or add more RAM

explanation: Memory near 100% slows Windows because it pages to disk. Close unneeded apps or add RAM, and look for leaking processes or malware.

scenario: A PC takes a long time to boot. Which tool helps disable unnecessary startup apps?
explanation: Startup apps in Task Manager can be disabled to reduce boot and sign-in time. Removing them doesn't uninstall them.

scenario: An application crashes every time it opens. What should be tried first?

options.note: Checks system files, not the app.

explanation: For an app that crashes on launch, check Event Viewer, then repair, update or reinstall the app. Reinstalling Windows is excessive.

scenario: A service needed by an app doesn't start at boot. Where should the technician look?
explanation: If a service won't start at boot, check services.msc for startup type, dependencies and the logon account, and Event Viewer for errors.

scenario: A user's PC clock keeps drifting and Kerberos sign-in errors appear. What should be checked?
explanation: Kerberos fails if clocks differ by more than about five minutes. Check time sync settings and the CMOS battery, and make sure the PC syncs with the domain controller.

scenario: After a Windows update, a PC won't boot properly. Which option can undo recent system changes without affecting personal files?

options.text: Reset this PC with Remove everything

explanation: System Restore returns system files, drivers and settings to an earlier restore point without touching personal documents. A reset or reinstall is more drastic.

scenario: Which recovery option reinstalls Windows but can keep personal files?

options.text: Reset this PC with Keep my files

explanation: Reset this PC with Keep my files reinstalls Windows, removes apps and settings, and keeps personal files. The Remove everything option wipes the user data.

scenario: A user's profile takes a very long time to load at sign-in. What could help?
explanation: Slow sign-in can come from a corrupt user profile. Create a new profile and migrate the data, or repair the existing one.

scenario: A browser keeps redirecting to unwanted sites and showing pop-ups. What is the likely cause?

options.note: Possible, but pop-ups point to malware.

explanation: Unwanted redirects and pop-ups usually come from a malicious extension or hijacked settings. Remove unknown extensions, reset the browser and scan for malware.

scenario: A user receives security alerts from an antivirus they never installed, asking them to pay. What is this?
explanation: Rogue antivirus is a scam that shows fake security alerts to extort payment. Don't pay or click, and follow the malware removal process.

scenario: Files have been renamed with strange extensions and can't be opened. What should be suspected?
explanation: Renamed files with odd extensions that can't open indicate ransomware. Isolate the device immediately and restore from clean backups.

scenario: A phone's battery drains fast and data usage is unusually high. Which security issue is likely?
explanation: Fast battery drain with unusual data use suggests a malicious background app. Check app permissions and data usage and remove suspicious apps.

scenario: A mobile app won't open or crashes on launch. What should be tried first?
explanation: If a mobile app crashes, force close it and update it, then clear the cache, reinstall or restart the device. Resetting the phone is a last resort.

scenario: Why is rooting or jailbreaking a phone a security risk?
explanation: Rooting or jailbreaking bypasses built-in security protections, allowing unapproved code and often blocking updates and warranty support. It raises malware risk.

scenario: Windows shows a "low disk space" warning on C:. What should be done first?
explanation: Disk Cleanup (or Storage Sense) removes temporary files and other clutter first. Then uninstall unused apps or move data before adding storage.

scenario: A program installed by a user keeps reinstalling itself after removal. What should be suspected?
explanation: Software that reinstalls itself after removal indicates malware with persistence. Check startup items, scheduled tasks and services, and run a full scan.

scenario: A user can't open a document because no app is associated with its file type. What should be done?

options.text: Set or install a default app

explanation: A file with no associated app needs a default app set or the right program installed. File associations map extensions to programs.

scenario: Which tool can be used to remove an app that won't uninstall normally on Windows?
explanation: Some apps won't uninstall normally and need the vendor's removal tool, which clears leftover files and registry entries. Check Event Viewer for errors too.

scenario: Windows displays "USB device not recognized" for a known-good flash drive. What should be tried first?

options.note: Checks the system drive, not USB.

explanation: For an unrecognized USB device, try another port, update or reinstall the driver, and check Device Manager. Power management can also turn off ports.

scenario: A user's email client keeps asking for a password after it was changed. What should be done?
explanation: If email keeps prompting after a password change, update the saved password in the client or Credential Manager, which may hold the old one.

scenario: An app displays an error about a missing DLL file. What should be tried first?

options.text: Download the DLL from a random website

explanation: A missing DLL error is usually fixed by repairing or reinstalling the application, which restores required files. Downloading DLLs from random sites risks malware.

scenario: A Windows PC restarts unexpectedly to install updates during work. How can this be prevented?

options.text: Set active hours or schedule restarts

explanation: Active hours or scheduled restarts stop Windows from rebooting during work for updates. Disabling updates entirely leaves the PC unpatched.

scenario: After a malware cleanup, what should the technician do to reduce the chance of reinfection?
explanation: User education is the final step in malware removal and reduces reinfection. Teach safe browsing, phishing awareness and not running unknown files.

scenario: A phone app requests access to contacts, location and SMS though it's only a flashlight. What should the user do?

options.text: Root the phone to control it
Move it to a different folder

explanation: A flashlight app asking for contacts, location and SMS is requesting excess permissions, a sign of malware. Deny them or uninstall the app.

scenario: A user reports the cursor moves on its own and files open by themselves. What should be suspected?
explanation: A cursor that moves on its own and files that open by themselves suggest a remote access trojan or an unauthorized remote session. Disconnect from the network and investigate.

scenario: A user's system time is wrong after every restart. Which hardware issue might cause this?
explanation: A clock that resets after restarts can mean a failing CMOS battery. Also check the time zone and time sync settings.

scenario: Which Windows feature boots with minimal drivers and services to troubleshoot problems?
explanation: Safe Mode starts Windows with minimal drivers and services to troubleshoot. Safe Mode with Networking also loads network drivers.

scenario: A user's apps are slow only when a nightly antivirus scan runs during work hours. What's a good fix?
explanation: Reschedule scans to off-hours if they slow users. This balances security and usability without disabling protection.

scenario: Before replacing a laptop's motherboard, what should a technician use to protect components?

options.text: An ESD strap connected to ground
A magnetic screwdriver on the board

explanation: Wear an ESD strap connected to ground when working on boards, and use mats and anti-static bags. Handle boards by the edges.

scenario: Which fire extinguisher type is safe for electrical fires?
explanation: A CO2 extinguisher (or Class C) is safe for electrical fires, since it leaves no residue and doesn't conduct. Water is dangerous on electrical fires. Remove power if safe.

scenario: Where should a technician find safe handling and disposal information for toner?
explanation: The Safety Data Sheet (SDS) explains hazards, handling, first aid and disposal for chemicals like toner. It is provided by the manufacturer.

scenario: How should old lithium-ion batteries be disposed of?

options.note: Still a fire hazard in trash.

explanation: Lithium-ion batteries must go to approved recycling or hazardous waste collection, never regular trash, because they can burn and leak toxic materials.

scenario: Which device keeps a server running briefly during a power outage so it can shut down safely?
explanation: A UPS provides battery power during an outage so servers can shut down safely, and it also conditions power. A surge protector doesn't supply power.

scenario: What is the correct way to lift a heavy server?

options.text: Lift with your legs, back straight
Bend at the waist and lift

explanation: Lift with your legs and a straight back, get help for heavy equipment or use a cart. Bending at the waist risks injury.

scenario: Which backup type copies only files changed since the last backup of any type?

options.note: Changes since the last full backup.

explanation: Incremental backups copy only files changed since the last backup of any type, so they are fast but restores need the full backup plus every incremental.

scenario: Which backup type copies all changes since the last FULL backup?

options.note: Since the last backup of any type.

explanation: Differential backups copy everything changed since the last full backup, so a restore needs only the full backup and the latest differential. Incremental needs the whole chain.

scenario: What does the 3-2-1 backup rule recommend?

options.text: 3 copies, on 2 types of media, with 1 offsite

explanation: The 3-2-1 rule means three copies, on two types of media, with one offsite. Test restores regularly because untested backups may fail.

scenario: Before making a major change to a production server, what should usually be approved?

options.text: A change request and rollback plan
A new asset tag for the server
A backup of the server only

explanation: Major changes to production need a documented change request with scope, risk analysis, a rollback plan and approval. Making changes without approval risks outages.

scenario: What is a rollback plan?

options.text: Steps to undo a change if it fails
A list of new features to add

explanation: A rollback plan gives the steps to undo a change if it fails and return to the previous working state. Always have one before changing production.

scenario: Which document records each IT support request and its resolution?

options.text: A ticket in the ticketing system
A sticky note on the monitor

explanation: A ticket in the ticketing system records the user, device, problem, steps taken, resolution and time spent. It gives an audit trail and helps with trends.

scenario: Which best describes professional communication with a frustrated customer?

options.text: Listen, stay calm and avoid arguing
Take personal calls during the visit

explanation: With a frustrated customer, listen actively, stay calm, avoid arguing or being defensive, clarify the issue, set expectations and follow up.

scenario: A technician sees confidential documents on a customer's desk during a repair. What should they do?

options.text: Ignore them and keep the information private
Read them to understand the business
Take a photo for the ticket

explanation: Respect customer privacy and confidentiality: don't read, copy or discuss what you see. Mention nothing about the contents to others.

scenario: Which describes personally identifiable information (PII)?

options.text: Data that can identify a person

explanation: PII is data that can identify a person, such as name, SSN or address. PHI and payment card data have extra rules (HIPAA, PCI DSS).

scenario: A technician finds illegal content on a work computer during a repair. What should they do?

options.text: Stop and follow the incident policy
Delete it and finish the repair
Copy it to a USB drive as proof
Ignore it and finish the repair

explanation: If illegal content is found, stop, don't investigate further, and follow the incident policy, preserving evidence and reporting to management or legal. Deleting it destroys evidence.

scenario: What is chain of custody?

options.text: A record of who handled evidence

explanation: Chain of custody documents who handled evidence, when and how, so it can be trusted in an investigation or court. Gaps can make evidence inadmissible.

scenario: Which license type allows anyone to view and modify the source code?
explanation: An open-source license lets anyone view, modify and share the code, subject to terms like attribution or sharing changes. Proprietary software licenses restrict this.

scenario: A user wants to install one software license on ten computers. What should the technician check?
explanation: Check the license terms (EULA) before installing one license on ten PCs. Installing beyond the license count violates it.

scenario: Which script file type runs in Windows PowerShell?
explanation: PowerShell scripts use .ps1. Others: .bat (batch), .vbs (VBScript), .js (JavaScript), .sh (shell) and .py (Python).

scenario: Which is a common, appropriate use of scripting for a help desk?
explanation: Scripting suits repetitive help desk tasks such as mapping drives, backups, restarts and gathering information. Test scripts before wide use.

scenario: What is a risk of running scripts from untrusted sources?

options.text: They always make PCs run faster

explanation: Scripts from untrusted sources may contain malware, so review them and test in a safe environment first. Running them as admin raises the risk.

scenario: Which remote access tool is built into Windows for controlling a desktop remotely?
explanation: Remote Desktop Connection (RDP) is built into Windows Pro and above to control a PC remotely. Other options: VNC, SSH, RMM tools and screen sharing, usually over a VPN.

scenario: Which tool lets an MSP monitor and manage many clients' computers from one console?
explanation: An RMM tool lets a managed service provider patch, monitor and support many clients' devices from one console. PSA tools handle ticketing and billing instead.

scenario: A user wants to paste customer records into a public AI chatbot to summarize them. What is the main concern?

options.text: The summary will be too short

explanation: Pasting customer records into a public AI tool risks exposing private data, because inputs may be stored or used for training. Follow company policy and use approved tools.

scenario: An AI tool gives a confident answer with a made-up command. What is this called?
explanation: An AI giving a confident but made-up answer is a hallucination. Verify AI output before using it, especially commands that change systems.

scenario: Which environmental control helps keep a server room safe for equipment?

options.text: Storing paper boxes next to racks

explanation: Server rooms need controlled temperature and humidity. Low humidity raises ESD risk and high humidity causes condensation and corrosion.

scenario: Why should cables in an office be managed with ties and covers?
explanation: Cable ties and covers prevent trips and cable damage, and improve airflow. Cable management is a safety matter, not just tidiness.
